quotes.text: You don't have a data problem. You have a conceptual one, mistaking intelligence infrastructure for storage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the core misconception the episode addresses.

quotes.text: Without semantic models, your data has no language. Without relationships, it has no memory. A CSV from sales, a CSV from marketing, a CSV from finance.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why raw files are unusable for AI reasoning.

quotes.text: Governance is meant to channel intelligence, not muzzle it. The brilliance of Fabric's model is in its proportionality, the balance between automation and accountability.

quotes.text: here's the litmus test. If your Fabric environment feels wild, you've undergoverned. If it feels paralyzed, you've overgoverned.

quotes.text: Your competitors aren't outrunning you with bigger data sets, they're outthinking you with the same data configured intelligently.

chapters.title: Your warehouse is a CSV graveyard
Data agents: the missing intelligence layer

takeaways: Dumping CSV snapshots into OneLake without semantic models or relationships leaves Fabric unable to support AI reasoning.
Fabric data agents, configured with semantic models, clear instructions and Copilot Studio integration, turn the warehouse into a system that detects trends and acts on them.
Purview, data loss prevention and lineage keep agents within governance boundaries so their conclusions stay traceable and auditable.
hook: Many organizations bought Microsoft Fabric for AI but use OneLake as a dumping ground for CSV exports. This episode shows data and analytics teams how semantic models, Fabric data agents and built-in governance turn a passive warehouse into a system that reasons over data and flags issues before anyone opens a dashboard.
